kangaskhan_dh.title: Mega Kangaskhan ex / Crustle — attack behind a two-axis wall
kangaskhan_dh.game_plan: Crustle is both the wall and the main attacker (65% of the deck's damage in the ladder games); Mega Kangaskhan ex draws from the Active Spot and closes. The defence works on two axes: Crustle prevents damage from attacks by the opponent's Pokémon ex, and Cornerstone Mask Ogerpon ex prevents damage from attacks by Pokémon that have an Ability. Grow Grass Energy and Hero's Cape raise the wall's HP and four Jumbo Ice Cream heal it, so prevention, HP and healing stack; four Boss's Orders pick the target.

targets.Crustle: Dragapult ex / Hydrapple ex / Lucario ex / Grimmsnarl ex — prevents damage from their attacks; other effects still apply
targets.Cornerstone Mask Ogerpon ex: the other axis: prevents damage from attacks by Pokémon that have an Ability. Demolish ignores effects on the target. Present in the mined list

hydrapple_k2.title: Hydrapple ex / Meganium / Teal Mask Ogerpon ex — double the energy, then hit
hydrapple_k2.game_plan: Meganium makes each Basic Grass Energy on your board provide two, and Hydrapple ex attaches one from hand each turn and heals 30, so Hydrapple ex's Syrup Storm (30 per Grass Energy on your side) and Teal Mask Ogerpon ex reach large damage quickly; Forest of Vitality lets either player's Grass Pokémon evolve the turn they are played, after turn one. This is the hybrid kind we saw winning the Lopunny matchup (Section 5, Case 3).

verification.by: user (PTCG domain review) + engine card text (data/EN_Card_Data.csv, exact printings from agents/<agent>/deck.csv)
corrections: Crustle: 'immune to damage from Pokémon ex' → damage from ATTACKS by opponent's Pokémon ex (effects are not prevented)
Battle Cage: 'no damage counters on benches' → only counters placed by EFFECTS of the opponent's attacks/Abilities, on both players' benches; attack damage still applies

Cornerstone Mask Ogerpon ex: the 'Fighting-type option vs Fighting-weak targets' rationale was WRONG — Demolish's damage is not affected by Weakness or Resistance. It is a second wall (blocks damage from attacks by Pokémon with an Ability) whose attack ignores effects on the target
Bayleef MEG 9: role 'gust' → forced switch; the OPPONENT chooses the replacement (unlike Boss's Orders)
Dipplin SCR 13: 'prevents damage next turn' → after Coated Attack, prevents damage from attacks by BASIC Pokémon during the opponent's next turn
Meowth ex POR 62: role 'draw' → searches a Supporter when played to the Bench
Mist / Rock Fighting Energy: prevent EFFECTS of the opponent's attacks on the holder; damage is not an effect
Forest of Vitality: applies to BOTH players and not on the first turn
Mega Meganium ex: +50 per Grass Energy attached to ITSELF
game_plan (Hydrapple): 'the hybrid that the winning lists used' → the hybrid kind observed in winning games (not an identical 60-card list)

wording (user review 2026-09-07): 'blocks attacks' → 'prevents damage from attacks'; the Kangaskhan defence is described as a two-axis wall (ex vs Ability) rather than two interchangeable walls; deck title uses the official name 'Teal Mask Ogerpon ex'

replay data (2026-09-13): Hydrapple ex re-labelled attacker (Syrup Storm = 68% of the deck's damage, Teal Mask Ogerpon ex 27%, Mega Meganium ex landed in 7.3% of games); Kangaskhan game plan states that Crustle deals 65% of the damage and Mega Kangaskhan ex closes; the Lopunny line no longer calls it 'our worst matchup' (Alakazam 34.0% is lower) and quotes both agents' ladder rates instead
